records.quote: Counterexample 3.1 Let Xi ∼ LL(σi, λi) and Yi ∼ LL(θi, λi), i = 1, 2, 3. Now, if (σ1, σ2, σ3) = (1, 1, 5) ∈ E+, (θ1, θ2, θ3) = (1, 2, 4) ∈ E+ and (λ1, λ2, λ3) = (4, 3, 0.2) ∈ D+ are taken, then from Figure 1, it is clear that F3:3(x)/G3:3(x) is not monotone, giving that X3:3 ≱rhr Y3:3, although σ ≽^m θ.
records.family: log-Lindley LL(σ, λ): f(x;σ,λ) = σ²/(1+λσ)(λ − log x)x^{σ−1}, 0 < x < 1
records.compared: σ = (1,1,5) vs θ = (1,2,4), common λ = (4,3,0.2); σ, θ ∈ E+ while λ ∈ D+ (mixed orderings)

hypotheses.formal: shape majorization holds but scale ordering is reversed (λ ∈ D+ vs σ,θ ∈ E+)

conclusion.direction: refuted: X3:3 ≱rhr Y3:3 — F3:3/G3:3 non-monotone although σ ≽^m θ

records.numbers: σ = (1,1,5); θ = (1,2,4); λ = (4,3,0.2); Figure 1 plots F3:3/G3:3 over (0,1), non-monotone
records.ambiguity: Shows the E+/D+ compatibility requirement in Theorem 3.1-type results is not dispensable; assessment is graphical (Figure 1) only.

note: Printed ≱rhr (crossed symbol in text layer) — non-monotone cdf ratio despite σ ≽^m θ; both passes' records substantively agree.

records.quote: Counterexample 3.2 Let Xi ∼ LL(σi, λi) and Yi ∼ (σi, δi), i = 1, 2, 3. Let (λ1, λ2, λ3) = (0.1, 0.3, 4.1) ∈ E+ and (δ1, δ2, δ3) = (0.2, 0.3, 4) ∈ E+, giving λ ≽^m δ. Now, if (σ1, σ2, σ3) = (0.1, 3, 5) ∈ E+ is taken, then Figure 2(a) shows that F3:3(x)/G3:3(x) is increasing in x. Again if (σ1, σ2, σ3) = (2, 3, 5) ∈ E+ is taken, then Figure 2(b) shows that F3:3(x)/G3:3(x) is decreasing in x. So, it can be concluded that, for all σ, λ, δ ∈ D+ (resp. E+), λ ≽^m δ does not always imply X3:3 ≤rhr Y3:3.
records.compared: λ = (0.1,0.3,4.1) vs δ = (0.2,0.3,4) with λ ≽^m δ; two common-σ choices (0.1,3,5) and (2,3,5) give opposite ratio monotonicity

hypotheses.text: λ, δ ∈ E+ with λ ≽^m δ; σ ∈ E+ in both trials
hypotheses.formal: scale majorization with shape vector common and similarly ordered

conclusion.direction: refuted as uniform claim: σ = (0.1,3,5) gives F/G increasing (X3:3 ≤rhr Y3:3 holds), σ = (2,3,5) gives F/G decreasing (X3:3 ≤rhr Y3:3 fails — opposite direction) — 'λ ≽^m δ does not always imply X3:3 ≤rhr Y3:3'

records.ambiguity: Prints 'Yi ∼ (σi, δi)' with the LL symbol dropped; graph-only evidence.

note: Two σ choices give opposite F/G monotonicity — direction ambiguity between passes is resolved by reading both sub-figures; printed conclusion verbatim.

records.quote: Theorem 3.4 For i = 1, 2, ..., n, let Xi and Yi be two sets of independent random variables each following the multiple-outlier EW model such that Xi ∼ LL(σ, λ) and Yi ∼ LL(θ, λ) for i = 1, 2, ..., n1, Xi ∼ LL(σ*, λ*) and Yi ∼ LL(θ*, λ*) for i = n1 + 1, n1 + 2, ..., n1 + n2 (= n). If (σ, σ, ..., σ, σ*, σ*, ..., σ*) ≽^m (θ, θ, ..., θ, θ*, θ*, ..., θ*) and either {σ ≥ σ*, θ ≥ θ*, λ ≥ λ*} or {σ ≤ σ*, θ ≤ θ*, λ ≤ λ*} then Xn:n ≥lr Yn:n.
